title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
authors: Rafael Rafailov*, Archit Sharma*, Eric Mitchell*, Stefano Ermon, Christopher D. Manning, Chelsea Finn (* equal contribution)
date: May 2023 (arXiv v1); v2 December 2023 (adds the CNN/DailyMail test); v3 July 2024

code.title: eric-mitchell/direct-preference-optimization
code.note: the authors' reference implementation, Apache 2.0; about 20 minutes for the README and the roughly 20-line preference_loss in trainers.py, which now also offers conservative DPO and IPO

takeaway: DPO collapses RLHF's reward-model-plus-PPO pipeline into one binary cross-entropy loss by reparameterising the reward as the policy/reference log-ratio, matching or beating PPO at 2023 scales.
verdict: Believe the derivation (it is exact) and the recipe (simple, cheap, adopted everywhere). Treat the head-to-head wins over PPO as suggestive rather than settled: each is a single run judged by GPT-4, the summarisation margin over PPO is about one standard error, and later controlled studies found well-tuned on-policy RL ahead on harder tasks.

headline.k: TL;DR win rate against the human reference summaries at temperature 0, DPO against PPO (GPT-4 judge)
headline.d: 158 and 146 of 256 prompts, read from the figure's vector data; about 1.1 standard errors apart

headline.k: IMDb sentiment: best true reward at KL ≤ 2, DPO against PPO with a learned reward
headline.d: 26 of PPO's 27 evaluation points are beaten by a DPO point on both axes

headline.k: drawn from the policy during training; PPO samples every step and keeps a reward model loaded
headline.d: 4 forward passes per pair, 2 of them cacheable

resources.n: the full derivation walked through step by step, plus where DPO sits in the modern post-training pipeline, with TRL code.
the production implementation: dataset format, the logged implicit-reward metrics (rewards/chosen, rewards/rejected, rewards/margins) and the catalogue of loss variants exposed as loss_type.

a textbook chapter on DPO and its descendants, with the derivation, the failure modes and the variants side by side.

2025: reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards at scale, the other pole of the DPO against online-RL debate.
